Hi all — quick technical note and minimal integration plan below. See attached code bundle for copy-paste snippets (acme_integration_snippets.zip).

1) SDK / auth
- Use Redwood JS SDK v1.4+ or REST API. SDK config example:
  const Redwood = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-west-2' });
- Auth: Bearer token in Authorization header; tokens are short-lived for POC and can be rotated.

2) API routes
- Generate (sync): POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  payload: { model: "rw-instruct-large-v1", input: "<user prompt>", max_tokens: 512 }
- Streaming: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?stream=true
  - Works over HTTP chunked responses. SDK exposes an async iterator when stream=true. Websocket option available for lower-latency bidirectional scenarios; we recommend HTTP streaming for the POC unless you need interactive typing latency <50ms.
- Tool-calling: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call_tool
  - Model returns a structured JSON { tool: "retriever", args: { query: "..." } } when it decides to call a tool. Redwood will emit a webhook to the tool endpoint you provide in the integration config.

3) Tool webhook security
- Redwood signs callbacks using HMAC-SHA256 with a per-POC secret. Verify using X-Redwood-Signature header. Example verification pseudo: verifySignature(body, header, secret).
- We can also proxy calls through your network if direct outbound is blocked.

4) Example streaming usage (pseudo-JS)
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?stream=true', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'rw-instruct-large-v1', input: userPrompt })
  });
  for await (const chunk of res.body) {
    // chunk is a piece of tokenized output; append to UI
  }

5) Minimal local test strategy
- Acme: run local retriever stub that responds to /tool/retriever with a static top-5 result set.
- Redwood: configure tool endpoint in the POC config to point at the stub and run an eval harness (we'll provide the harness script).

6) Performance notes / limits for POC
- Default token limit: 4096; we recommend initial context <= 2k tokens for stable KV cache behavior.
- If you plan to stream many small messages concurrently, let us know expected QPS — we can bump reservations for the trial.

I'll attach the snippets and a minimal harness. Ping me if you want a short screen-share to walk through the sample.

—Dev Patel
